articleTitle: Derived categories of resolutions of cyclic quotient singularities
abstract: For a cyclic group G acting on a smooth variety X with only one character occurring in the G-equivariant decomposition of the normal bundle of the fixed point locus, we study the derived categories of the orbifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[{X/G}]$</tex> and the blow-up resolution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\tilde {Y}} \to X/G$</tex>. Some results generalize known facts about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X = {{\BBA}^n}$</tex> with diagonal G-action, while other results are new also in this basic case. In particular, if the codimension of the fixed point locus equals <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|G|$</tex>, we study the induced tensor products under the equivalence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\rm {D}}^{\rm {b}}}\,( {\tilde Y}) \cong \,{{\rm {D}}^{{\rm {b}}\,}}({[ {X/G}]})$</tex> and give a ‘flop–flop = twist’ type formula. We also introduce candidates for general constructions of categorical crepant resolutions inside the derived category of a given geometric resolution of singularities and test these candidates on cyclic quotient singularities.

articleTitle: Metric semigroups that determine locally compact groups
abstract: Let G be a locally compact group. Let A be any one of the (complex) Banach algebras: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${L^1}(G)$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M(G)$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {WAP}}(G)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm {LUC}}(G)$</tex>, consisting of integrable functions, regular Borel complex measures, weakly almost periodic functions and bounded left uniformly continuous functions, respectively, on G. We show that the metric semigroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{+}^{1}: = \{{f \in A:f \geqslant 0 \ {\rm {and}} \ \parallel f\parallel = 1}\}$</tex> (the convex structure is not considered) is a complete invariant for G.

articleTitle: Envelopes of legendre curves in the unit spherical bundle over the unit sphere
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a one-parameter family of Legendre curves in the unit spherical bundle over the unit sphere and the curvature. We give the existence and uniqueness theorems for one-parameter families of spherical Legendre curves by using the curvatures. Then we define an envelope for the one-parameter family of Legendre curves in the unit spherical bundle. We also consider the parallel curves and evolutes of one-parameter families of Legendre curves in the unit spherical bundle and their envelopes. Moreover, we give relationships among one-parameter families of Legendre curves in the unit spherical bundle over the unit sphere and one-parameter families of Legendre curves in the unit tangent bundle over the Euclidean plane.

articleTitle: Shi-type estimates and finite time singularities of flows of G2 structures
abstract: In this paper, we extend Lotay–Wei’s Shi-type estimate from Laplacian flow to more general flows of G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> structures including the modified Laplacian co-flow. Then we prove a version of κ-non-collapsing theorem. We will use both of them to study finite-time singularities of general flows of G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> structures.

articleTitle: Secondary Upsilon invariants of knots
abstract: The knot invariant Upsilon, defined by Ozsváth, Stipsicz and Szabó, induces a homomorphism from the smooth knot concordance group to the group of piecewise linear functions on the interval [0, 2]. Here we define a set of related secondary invariants, each of which assigns to a knot a piecewise linear function on [0, 2]. These secondary invariants provide bounds on the genus and concordance genus of knots. Examples of knots for which Upsilon vanishes, but which are detected by these secondary invariants are presented.

articleTitle: On the pairwise maxima of generalised divisor functions
abstract: In this paper, we prove the asymptotic growth rate of the summatory function of the pairwise maxima of the generalized divisor function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_{k}(n)$</tex>, for a fixed positive integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k \geq 2$</tex>. This result generalizes previous results of Kátai, Erdős and Hall on the local behaviour of divisor function on short intervals.

articleTitle: The third moment of symmetric square L-functions
abstract: We prove an asymptotic for the third moment of symmetric-square L-functions associated to holomorphic Hecke cusp forms of level one and weight between K and 2K, as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K \rightarrow \infty$</tex>.

articleTitle: Autour des plus grands facteurs premiers d’entiers consÉcutifs voisins d’un entier criblÉ
abstract: Denote by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P^+(n)$</tex> (resp. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P^-(n)$</tex>) the largest (resp. the smallest) prime factor of the integer n. In this paper, we prove that there exists a positive proportion of integers n having no small prime factor such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P^+(n) < P^+(n+2)$</tex>. Especially, we prove that the pattern <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P^+ ({P_3 }) < P^+(P_3 + 2)$</tex> is realized by a positive proportion of P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P - ({P_3 }) > x^{1/3-\delta}, 0 < \delta \leq \frac{1}{12}$</tex>, where P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> denote an integer having at most three prime factors taken with multiplicity. We also prove that the pattern <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P^+(P-1) < P^+(P+1)$</tex> holds for a positive proportion of primes under the Elliott-Halberstam conjecture.

articleTitle: Groups with boundedly finite conjugacy classes of commutators
abstract: In 1954, B.H. Neumann discovered that if G is a group in which all conjugacy classes are finite with bounded size, then the derived group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${G}'$</tex> is finite. Later (in 1957), Wiegold found an explicit bound for the order of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${G}'$</tex>. We study groups in which the conjugacy classes containing commutators are finite with bounded size. We obtain the following results. Let G be a group and n a positive integer. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mid{x}^G\mid \leq n$</tex> for any commutator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x \in G$</tex>, then the second derived group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${G}''$</tex> is finite with n-bounded order. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mid{x}^{{G}'}\mid \leq n$</tex> for any commutator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x \in G$</tex>, then the order of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma_{3}({G}')$</tex> is finite and n-bounded.

articleTitle: Geometric interpolation of entropy numbers
abstract: We investigate whether the entropy numbers of an operator behave well under the complex interpolation between Hilbert spaces. We study geometric interpolation of entropy numbers of operators. We deliver a contribution to this problem by showing that an interpolation type inequality holds for these numbers. This is in contrast to the situation in Banach spaces, where by examples of Edmunds and Netrusov the entropy numbers do not interpolate well at least in the situation of the real method. As an application, we also present an interpolation estimate of single eigenvalues by single entropy numbers.

articleTitle: Linear equations with rational fractions of bounded height and stochastic matrices
abstract: We obtain a tight, up to a logarithmic factor, upper bound on the number of solutions to the equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\mathop {\mathop \sum}_{j = 1}^n {a_j}{{{s_j}} \over {{r_j}}} = {a_0},$$</tex> with variables <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${r_1}, \ldots ,{r_n}$</tex> in an arbitrary box at the origin and variables <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${s_1}, \ldots ,{s_n}$</tex> in an essentially arbitrary translation of this box. We apply this result to get an upper bound on the number of stochastic matrices with rational entries of bounded height.

articleTitle: Gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta-function
abstract: We prove that there exist infinitely many consecutive zeros of the Riemann zeta-function on the critical line whose gaps are greater than 3.18 times the average spacing. Using a modification of our method, we also show that there are even larger gaps between the multiple zeros of the Riemann zeta-function on the critical line (if such zeros exist).

articleTitle: Incomplete gauss sums modulo primes
abstract: We obtain a new bound for incomplete Gauss sums modulo primes. Our argument falls under the framework of Vinogradov’s method which we use to reduce the problem under consideration to bounding the number of solutions to two distinct systems of congruences. The first is related to Vinogradov’s mean value theorem, although the second does not appear to have been considered before. Our bound improves on current results in the range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N \geqslant {q^{2{k^{- 1/2}} + O({{k^{ - 3/2}}})}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: On congruences involving products of variables from short intervals
abstract: We prove several results which imply the following consequences. For any ε > 0 and any sufficiently large prime p, if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{I}_{1}, …, \mathcal{I}_{13}$</tex> are intervals of cardinalities <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mid\mathcal{I_{j}}\mid > p^{1/4+\varepsilon}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$abc \not\equiv 0(mod p)$</tex>, then the congruence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$ax_1 … x_6 + bx_7 … x_{13} \equiv c (mod \textit{p})$$</tex> has a solution with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_j \in \mathcal{I_j}$</tex>. There exists an absolute constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n_0 \in \mathbb{N}$</tex> such that for any 0 < ε < 1 and any sufficiently large prime p, any quadratic residue λ modulo p can be represented in the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_1 … x_{n0} \equiv\lambda$</tex> (mod p), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_i \in \mathbb{N}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_i \leq p^{1/(4e^{2/3})+\varepsilon}$</tex>. For any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon > 0$</tex>, there exists <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n = n(\varepsilon) \in \mathbb{N}$</tex> such that for any sufficiently large <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m \in \mathbb{N}$</tex> the congruence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_1 … x_{n} \equiv 1$</tex> (mod m), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_{i} \in \mathbb{N}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_i \leq m^{\varepsilon}$</tex> has a solution with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_1 \neq 1$</tex>.

articleTitle: Homological finiteness properties of fibre products
abstract: We study the homological finiteness property FP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> of fibre products. A homological version of the n − (n + 1) − (n + 2) Conjecture is suggested and solved in some cases. Though the Homological 1–2–3 Conjecture is still open, we prove a homological version of the Virtual Surjection Conjecture in the case of virtual surjection on pairs.

articleTitle: The radical of the bidual of a Beurling algebra
abstract: We prove that the bidual of a Beurling algebra on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}$</tex>, considered as a Banach algebra with the first Arens product, can never be semisimple. We then show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$rad(\ell^1(\oplus_{i=1}^{\infty} \mathbb{Z})")$</tex> contains nilpotent elements of every index. Each of these results settles a question of Dales and Lau. Finally we show that there exists a weight ω on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}$</tex> such that the bidual of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell^{1}(\mathbb{Z}, \omega)$</tex> contains a radical element which is not nilpotent.

articleTitle: The aliquot constant, after Bosma and Kane
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s(n)$</tex> be the sum of those positive divisors of the natural number n other than n itself. A conjecture of Catalan–Dickson is that the ‘aliquot’ sequence of iterating s starting at any n terminates at 0 or enters a cycle. There is a ‘counter’ conjecture of Guy–Selfridge that while Catalan–Dickson may be correct for most odd numbers n, for most even seeds, the aliquot sequence is unbounded. Lending some support for Catalan–Dickson, Bosma and Kane recently showed that the geometric mean of the numbers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s(n)/n$</tex> for n even tends to a constant smaller than 1. In this paper, we reprove their result with a stronger error term and with a finer calculation of the asymptotic geometric mean. In addition, we solve the analogous problems for certain subsets of the even numbers, such as the even squarefrees and the multiples of 4.

articleTitle: Epimorphisms of 3-manifold groups
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f: M \rightarrow N$</tex> be a proper map between two aspherical compact orientable 3-manifolds with empty or toroidal boundary. We assume that N is not a closed graph manifold. Suppose that f induces an epimorphism on fundamental groups. We show that f is homotopic to a homeomorphism if one of the following holds: either for any finite-index subgroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi_{1}{(N)}$</tex> the ranks of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> and of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{*}^{-1}(\Gamma)$</tex> agree, or for any finite cover <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde{N}$</tex> of N the Heegaard genus of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde{N}$</tex> and the Heegaard genus of the pull-back cover <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde{M}$</tex> agree.

articleTitle: On (k, n)-absorbing hyperideals in Krasner (m, n)-hyperrings*
abstract: Krasner Hyperrings are an important class of algebraic hyperstructures which generalize rings further to allow multiple output values for the addition operation. Krasner (m, n)-hyperrings are a generalization of canonical n-ary hypergroups, a generalization of (m, n)-rings, a generalizations of hyperrings in the sense of Krasner and a subclass of the (m, n)-hyperrings. Badawi introduced a generalization of prime ideals called 2-absorbing ideals and this idea is further generalized in a paper by Anderson and Badawi to a concept called n-absorbing ideals. In this paper, we generalize this notion in Krasner (m, n)-hyperrings introducing and studying the notion of (k, n)-absorbing hyperideal. Several properties of them are provided. Also we introduce the notion of (k, n)-absorbing primary hyperideals of H generalizing the analogs results obtained in rings. Several properties of them are provided.

articleTitle: Locally finite derivations and modular coinvariants
abstract: We consider a finite-dimensional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {K}G$</tex>-module V of a p-group G over a field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {K}$</tex> of characteristic p. We describe a generating set for the corresponding Hilbert Ideal. In case G is cyclic, this yields that the algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {K}[V]_G$</tex> of coinvariants is a free module over its subalgebra generated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {K}G$</tex>-module generators of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V*$</tex>. This subalgebra is a quotient of a polynomial ring by pure powers of its variables. The coinvariant ring was known to have this property only when G was cyclic of prime order [M. Sezer, Decomposing modular coinvariants, J. Algebra423 (2015), 87–92]. In addition, we show that if G is the Klein 4-group and V does not contain an indecomposable summand isomorphic to the regular module, then the Hilbert Ideal is a complete intersection, extending a result of the second author and Shank [M. Sezer and R. J. Shank, Rings of invariants for modular representations of the Klein four group, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 368 (2016), 5655–5673].

articleTitle: Irreducible compositions of degree two polynomials over finite fields have regular structure
abstract: Let q be an odd prime power and D be the set of irreducible polynomials in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {F}_{q}[x]$</tex> which can be written as a composition of degree two polynomials. In this paper, we prove that D has a natural regular structure by showing that there exists a finite automaton having D as accepted language. Our method is constructive.

articleTitle: On abelian multiplicatively dependent points on a curve in a torus
abstract: We show, under some natural conditions, that the set of abelian (and thus also cyclotomic) multiplicatively dependent points on an irreducible curve over a number field is a finite union of preimages of roots of unity by a certain finite set of primitive characters from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBG}_{\rm {m}}^n$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBG}_{\rm {m}}}$</tex> restricted to the curve, and a finite set. We also introduce the notion of primitive multiplicative dependence and obtain a finiteness result for primitively multiplicatively dependent points defined over a so-called Bogomolov extension of a number field.

articleTitle: On growth conditions for quasiconvex integrands
abstract: We prove that, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \leqslant p < 2$</tex>, if a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${W^{1,p}}$</tex>-quasiconvex integrand <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f:{{\BBR}^{N \times n}} \to {\BBR}$</tex> has linear growth from above on the rank-one cone, then it must satisfy this growth for all matrices in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBR}^{N \times n}}$</tex>. An immediate corollary of this is, for example, that there can be no quasiconvex integrand that has genuinely superlinear p growth from above for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 < p < 2$</tex>, but only linear growth in rank-one directions. This result was first anticipated in (P. Soneji, Relaxation in BV of integrals with superlinear growth, ESAIM Control Optim. Calc. Var. 20 (2014), 1078–1122), with some partial results given. The key element of this proof involves constructing a Sobolev function which maps points in a cube to some one-dimensional frame, and, moreover, preserves boundary values. This construction is an inductive process on the dimension n, and involves using a Whitney decomposition. This technique also allows us to generalize this result for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${W^{1,p}}$</tex>-quasiconvex integrands, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \leqslant p < k \leqslant \, \min \, \{ {n,N} \}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Inflection points on hyperbolic tori of ${{\BBS}^3}$
abstract: Families of hyperbolic tori in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBS}^3}$</tex> (the asymptotic lines are globally defined) without double inflection points is provided. More precisely, a small deformation of the Clifford torus para-metrized by asymptotic lines is analyzed, and it is described the set of inflections of the two families of asymptotic lines <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal {A}}_1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal {A}}_2}$</tex>. Denote by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal {I}}_i}$</tex> the set of inflections of the asymptotic lines of the associated asymptotic foliation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal {A}}_i}$</tex>, also called flecnodal set. The intersection <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal I}_1} \cap {{\cal I}_2}$</tex> is called the set of double inflections. It is shown that by an appropriated deformation of the Clifford torus the set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\cal I}_1} \cap {{\cal I}_2}$</tex> is empty for the deformed surface. This gives a negative answer to a problem formulated by S. Tabachnikov and V. Ovsienko [Hyperbolic Carathéodory Conjecture, Proc. of the Steklo Inst. of Math. 258 (2007), pp. 178–193] in the context of spherical surfaces. Also, a family of immersed tori in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\BBS}^3}$</tex>, without double inflection set, is obtained.

articleTitle: Left-invariant grauert tubes on SU(2)
abstract: Let M be a real analytic Riemannian manifold. An adapted complex structure on TM is a complex structure on a neighborhood of the zero section such that the leaves of the Riemann foliation are complex submanifolds. This structure is called entire if it may be extended to the whole of TM. We call such manifolds Grauert tubes, or simply tubes. We consider here the case of M = G a compact connected Lie group with a left-invariant metric, and try to determine for which such metrics the associated tube is entire. It is well known that the Grauert tube of a bi-invariant metric on a Lie group is entire. The case of the smallest group SU(2) is treated completely, thanks to the complete integrability of the geodesic flow for such a metric, a standard result in classical mechanics. Along the way we find a new obstruction to tubes being entire which is made visible by the complete integrability.

articleTitle: Diagonal automorphisms of the 2-adic ring C*-algebra
abstract: The 2-adic ring C*-algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{Q_2}$</tex> naturally contains a copy of the Cuntz algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O_2}$</tex> and, a fortiori, also of its diagonal subalgebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{D_2}$</tex> with Cantor spectrum. This paper is aimed at studying the group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Aut_{\mathcal{D_2}}{(\mathcal{Q_2})}$</tex> of the automorphisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{Q_2}$</tex> fixing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{D_2}$</tex> pointwise. It turns out that any such automorphism leaves <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O_2}$</tex> globally invariant. Furthermore, the subgroup <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Aut_{\mathcal{D_2}}{(\mathcal{Q_2})}$</tex> is shown to be maximal abelian in Aut<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathcal{Q_2})$</tex>. Saying exactly what the group is amounts to understanding when an automorphism of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O_2}$</tex> that fixes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{D_2}$</tex> pointwise extends to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{Q_2}$</tex>. A complete answer is given for all localized automorphisms: these will extend if and only if they are the composition of a localized inner automorphism with a gauge automorphism.

articleTitle: The Morse–Sard Theorem revisited
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n, m, k$</tex> be positive integers with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k = n − m + 1$</tex>. We establish an abstract Morse–Sard-type theorem which allows us to deduce, on the one hand, a previous result of De Pascale’s for Sobolev <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W_{loc}^{k,p}(\mathbb{R}^n, \mathbb{R}^m)$</tex> functions with p > n and, on the other hand, also some new results such as the following: if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f \in C^{k-1}(\mathbb{R}^n, \mathbb{R}^m)$</tex> satisfies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\mathop{\lim\,sup}_{h\rightarrow0}{\vert D^{k-1}f(x+h)-D^{k-1}f(x)\vert \over\vert h \vert} < \infty $$</tex> for every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x \in \mathbb{R}^n$</tex> (that is, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D^{k-1}f$</tex> is a Stepanov function), then the set of critical values of f is Lebesgue-null in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^m$</tex>. In the case that m = 1 we also show that this limiting condition holding for every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x \in {\BBR}^{n} \backslash {\cal N}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal N}$</tex> is a set of zero (n − 2 + α)-dimensional Hausdorff measure for some 0 < α < 1 is sufficient to guarantee the same conclusion.

articleTitle: The singularity category of a quadratic monomial algebra*
abstract: We exploit singular equivalences between artin algebras that are induced from certain functors between the stable module categories. Such functors are called pre-triangle equivalences. We construct two pre-triangle equivalences connecting the stable module category over a quadratic monomial algebra to the one over an algebra with radical square zero. Consequently, we obtain an explicit singular equivalence between the two algebras. It turns out that this singular equivalence restricts to a triangle equivalence between their stable categories of Gorenstein-projective modules, and thus induces a triangle equivalence between their Gorenstein defect categories.

articleTitle: Equivariant embeddings of rational homology balls
abstract: We generalize theorems of Khodorovskiy and Park–Park–Shin, and give new topological proofs of those theorems, using embedded surfaces in the 4-ball and branched double covers. These theorems exhibit smooth codimension-zero embeddings of certain rational homology balls bounded by lens spaces.

articleTitle: Conjectures uniformes sur les variétés abéliennes
abstract: We consider several conjectures on abelian varieties over number fields whose common feature is a bound that depends only on the dimension of the variety and the degree of the number field. For example, Coleman’s conjecture predicts that only a finite number of rings can occur as endomorphism rings once these two parameters are fixed. We show that this conjecture implies the existence of a small polarization as well as a uniform isogeny conjecture (without Faltings height) which in turn implies the uniform torsion conjecture. We then discuss several variants of the Lang–Silverman conjecture on heights and implications between them. In particular, we show how a rather weak version is, under Coleman’s conjecture, equivalent to much more precise versions. We build on Bertrand’s work to give a bound explicit in terms of the polarization.

articleTitle: Hodge theory on transversely symplectic foliations
abstract: In this paper, we develop symplectic Hodge theory on transversely symplectic foliations. In particular, we establish the symplectic dδ-lemma for any such foliations with the (transverse) s-Lefschetz property. As transversely symplectic foliations include many geometric structures, such as contact manifolds, co-symplectic manifolds, symplectic orbifolds and symplectic quasi-folds as special examples, our work provides a unifying treatment of symplectic Hodge theory in these geometries. As an application, we show that on compact K-contact manifolds, the s-Lefschetz property implies a general result on the vanishing of cup products, and that the cup length of a 2n + 1 dimensional compact K-contact manifold with the (transverse) s-Lefschetz property is at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2n - s$</tex>. For any even integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s \geqslant 2$</tex>, we also apply our main result to produce examples of K-contact manifolds that are s-Lefschetz, but not <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(s + 1)$</tex>-Lefschetz.

articleTitle: Quotients of hyperelliptic curves and Étale cohomology
abstract: We study hyperelliptic curves C with an action of an affine group of automorphisms G. We establish a closed form expression for the quotient curve C/G and for the first étale cohomology group of C as a representation of G. The motivation comes from the arithmetic of hyperelliptic curves over local fields, specifically their local Galois representations and the associated invariants.

articleTitle: On the image of the parabolic Hitchin map
abstract: We determine the image of the (strongly) parabolic Hitchin map for all parabolics in classical groups and G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Surprisingly, we find that the image is isomorphic to an affine space in all cases, except for certain ‘bad parabolics’ in type D, where the image can be singular.

articleTitle: Preduals of JBW*-triples are 1-Plichko spaces
abstract: We investigate the preduals of JBW<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>-triples from the point of view of Banach space theory. We show that the algebraic structure of a JBW<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>-triple M naturally yields a decomposition of its predual M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</inf>, by showing that M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</inf> is a 1-Plichko space (that is, it admits a countably 1-norming Markushevich basis). In case M is σ-finite, its predual M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</inf> is even weakly compactly generated. These results are a common roof for previous results on L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>-spaces, preduals of von Neumann algebras, and preduals of JBW<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>-algebras.

articleTitle: Loewy lengths of centers of blocks
abstract: Let B be a block of a finite group with respect to an algebraically closed field F of characteristic p > 0. In a recent paper, Otokita gave an upper bound for the Loewy length LL(ZB) of the center ZB of B in terms of a defect group D of B. We refine his methods in order to prove the optimal bound LL(ZB) ≤ LL(FD) whenever D is abelian. We also improve Otokita’s bound for non-abelian defect groups. As an application, we classify the blocks B such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$LL(ZB) \geq \mid{D}\mid/2$</tex>.

articleTitle: Étale homological stability and arithmetic statistics
abstract: We relate asymptotic point counts and arithmetic statistics over finite fields to homological stability and representation stability over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{C}$</tex> in the example of configuration spaces of n points on smooth varieties. In order to accomplish this, we establish subexponential bounds on the growth of the unstable cohomology of such spaces. We apply this and étale homological stability to compute the large n limits of various arithmetic statistics of configuration spaces of varieties over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {F}_q$</tex>.

articleTitle: Complexities of 3-manifolds from triangulations, Heegard splittings, and surgery presentations
abstract: We study complexities of 3-manifolds defined from triangulations, Heegaard splittings, and surgery presentations. We show that these complexities are related by linear inequalities, by presenting explicit geometric constructions. We also show that our linear inequalities are asymptotically optimal. Our results are used in another paper of the author to estimate Cheeger-Gromov L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>ρ-invariants in terms of geometric group theoretic and knot theoretic data.

articleTitle: AR-Components of domestic finite group schemes: McKay-Quivers and Ramification
abstract: For a domestic finite group scheme, we give a direct description of the Euclidean components in its Auslander–Reiten quiver via the McKay-quiver of a finite linearly reductive subgroup scheme of SL(2). Moreover, for a normal subgroup scheme <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {N}}$</tex> of a finite group scheme <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal {G}}$</tex>, we show that there is a connection between the ramification indices of the restriction morphism <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\BBP}({{\cal {V}}_{\cal {N}}}) \to {\BBP}({{\cal {V}}_{\cal {G}}})$</tex> between their projectivized cohomological support varieties and the ranks of the tubes in their Auslander–Reiten quivers.

articleTitle: The γ-filtration on the Witt ring of a scheme
abstract: The K-ring of symmetric vector bundles over a scheme X, the so-called Grothendieck–Witt ring of X, can be endowed with the structure of a (special) λ-ring. The associated γ-filtration generalizes the fundamental filtration on the (Grothendieck–)Witt ring of a field and is closely related to the ‘classical’ filtration by the kernels of the first two Stiefel–Whitney classes.
